info.title: Open Energy Data Layer — Philippine Electricity Rates Data API
info.summary: Static, read-only JSON API over the DOE Electricity Rates & Power Market Monitor workbook.
info.description:
Production OpenAPI 3.1 contract for the static, read-only energy-data API built from the
Department of Energy (DOE) **Electricity Rates & Power Market Monitor** workbook by
`tools/build-api.py`. The contract matches the emitted files under `draft/api/v1/` exactly:
19 routes over 318 JSON files, no invented endpoints. Every route's `x-static-file` names
the file that serves it; the four per-entity route families (utilities, service areas,
regions, sources) point at a concrete example file because the served URL is the path
template in the operation path (`/utilities/{code}.json`, `/service-areas/{code}.json`,
`/regions/{psgc}.json`, `/sources/{source_id}.json`).

**Source.** Department of Energy (DOE), *Electricity Rates & Power Market Monitor*
(https://doe.gov.ph/data-and-prices/electricity), retrieved 2026-11-10T17:00:34+08:00 by CSV
export of the public Google Sheet. The dataset covers 141 distribution utilities and electric
cooperatives, 18 PSA PSGC regions and 107 monthly columns (2018-01 to 2026-11; the latest
published month is 2026-10). Every value resolves to a source row and a per-tab SHA-256; the
full record is in `/sources.json`.

**Units.** Every rate is the published monthly average in **PHP per kWh**
(`currency: "PHP"`, `unit: "PHP per kWh"` in each response's `meta`). There is no rescaling:
the two decimals are the source's own. NDA, missing and invalid source cells are published as
explicit states — never as zero, never imputed, never modelled.

**Service areas.** The dataset also publishes a provider service-area (coverage) layer for
the map's provider filter: one row per utility x covered LGU where sourced, barangay-level
rows where the franchise is barangay-only, and a single region-level fallback row where no
LGU-level service area is available. Coverage is **derived data, not a DOE rate
publication**: a franchise/service area is not verified household-level billing territory,
and region-level rows are an explicit fallback, not LGU-level confirmation. Sources are
published with the rows and carry their own licences: RA 12146 (public law) for MERALCO,
the DOE workbook region column for the fallback (terms unconfirmed), and — where present —
the OpenStreetMap Wiki operator table (CC BY-SA 2.0) and the Wikipedia distribution-utility
list (CC BY-SA 4.0), both requiring attribution and share-alike. Because the layer merges
those CC BY-SA rows with the public-law MERALCO area, **the combined coverage layer is a
CC BY-SA derivative**: attribution is required and share-alike applies to redistributed
coverage data (the DOE rate data is unaffected). See `/service-areas.json` and the
`disclaimer-coverage` disclaimer.

**Access.** These are static JSON files: GET and HEAD only, no authentication, no API key and
no request body. When served by the deployment host they SHOULD carry
`Cache-Control: public, max-age=300, s-maxage=3600` and open CORS
(`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`), following the BetterGov Budget API convention
(https://budget.bettergov.ph/api); each file is immutable within a `dataset_version`, so
aggressive client-side caching is safe. Identify heavy automated use with a descriptive
`User-Agent` (fair use). This is a dated snapshot, not a live service.

**Base URL.** The server URL is relative (`api/v1`, no leading slash): it resolves against
the location of this document, not the host root. The canonical origin is set at deployment
and no domain is invented here: the spec is `draft/openapi.yaml`, the files are served under
`draft/api/v1/`, and a page links to them relatively (e.g. `api/v1/meta.json`).

**Envelope and pagination.** Every data file returns
`{ "meta": ..., "data": ..., "next_cursor": null }`. `meta` states api_version,
dataset_version, latest_month, generated_at, source, attribution, licence and disclaimers,
plus `count`. `next_cursor` is always null: a static snapshot has no query layer or page
size. The field is reserved so a future dynamic deployment can paginate without breaking
clients. `index.json` (the catalog) and `openapi.json` (this document) are not envelopes.

**Versioning.** `api_version` ("1.0") is the JSON contract version; `dataset_version`
("2026-11-10") is the retrieval date and changes with every new snapshot. Files are never
silently rewritten inside one dataset_version. See `x-changelog`.

**Licence.** The upstream DOE workbook is not stated by publisher: it carries no explicit
reuse licence, so the data is served with licence status "Not stated by publisher". No
licence is asserted over the upstream data; reuse terms are to be confirmed with DOE in
writing. Do not presume an open licence for these figures.

**Disclaimers.** Every response carries the same five disclaimers, quoted in full below in
the `Meta` schema and visible in any response's `meta.disclaimers`:
`disclaimer-unofficial` (not an official DOE publication — verify against the source),
`disclaimer-licence` (upstream rate-data reuse terms unconfirmed),
`disclaimer-nda` (NDA / missing / invalid are preserved, never imputed),
`disclaimer-rates` (monthly averages; not financial advice) and
`disclaimer-coverage` (coverage is derived data, not a DOE rate publication, and is not
verified billing territory). Keep them with any figure you republish. Attribution:
Department of Energy (DOE) as the rate-data source; each coverage source as recorded in
`meta.service_area.sources`; the Open Energy Data Layer for the compilation.

get.summary: Dataset metadata: source, licence, coverage, identifiers, checksums
get.description:
The full dataset metadata document: rate coverage, units, identifier schemes, the
status vocabulary, the complete rate-source record, licence status, disclaimers, the
service-area coverage block (stats, sources, checks, files), SHA-256 checksums of the six
seed data files, archived raw snapshots and links to every machine-readable artefact.
This is the file to read first when onboarding to the dataset.

200.description: Dataset metadata document. Full response: api/v1/meta.json.

get.summary: Snapshot health: build identity and the data-quality check result
get.description:
Build identity plus the result of the recorded data-quality checks (17 rate checks and
the coverage checks). `status: "ok"` means the published snapshot is internally
consistent and every recorded check passes; it is not an uptime or live-service signal.
A failed check would set the status to `degraded` and the individual checks are always
readable at `/validation.json`.

get.summary: The 17 data-quality checks run against the retrieved workbook
get.description:
Row counts, month coverage, known spot values, derived aggregates and checksum checks, as
run at retrieval time and published verbatim, plus the separate coverage checks that
validate the service-area layer. In this snapshot every check passes; a failure would set
`/health.json` status to `degraded`.

get.summary: Source disagreements, with the resolution rule
get.description:
Rows where the workbook's four tabs disagree: region, island-group and grid-connection
conflicts, plus name variants. Resolved by tab majority where a majority exists; a 2-2
grid split is published as `CONFLICT` rather than guessed.

get.summary: Index of the latest published month per customer class
get.description:
Points at the four per-class files for 2026-10 with their summary statistics, sizes and
SHA-256 checksums. Start here for one customer class; use `/utilities/{code}.json` for
one utility's full history.

get.summary: One utility with its full monthly series per customer class
get.description:
The registry record, all four customer-class series for one utility (grouped by
explicit source state: `published` maps month to PHP/kWh, while `nda`, `missing` and
`invalid` list the months with those states) and the full `service_area` coverage block
(provinces, LGU codes, barangays, source ids). All four series states together cover every
month in `coverage.months_total` exactly once. Codes come from `/utilities.json`; an
unknown code is simply not a file (the host returns 404). There is one file per code
(`api/v1/utilities/<CODE>.json`, 141 files); `x-static-file` names the MERALCO example.

200.description: One utility with series. Full response: api/v1/utilities/MERALCO.json.

get.summary: Provider service-area coverage registry, with source records
get.description:
One item per utility with a compact coverage summary (`detail`, `source_ids`, `regions`,
`lgu_count`, `province_count`, `barangay_count`), the coverage-source registry
(franchise law, DOE region fallback, OSM Wiki / Wikipedia tables) with each source's
licence, attribution and `used_for` counts, and the aggregate coverage statistics.
`coverage.detail` says the strongest published level; `coverage.regions` lists every
PSGC region the published rows touch, so a multi-region franchise is visible even when
the DOE workbook lists one region. Coverage is derived data, not a DOE rate publication.

get.summary: One utility's full service-area coverage rows
get.description:
The published coverage rows for one utility, each carrying its `source_id`, area level
(`lgu`, `barangay` or `region`), the PSGC hierarchy (region, province, `adm3`, `adm4`)
and the source's `coverage_note`; plus the full coverage summary block (provinces, LGU
codes, barangays) and the source records used by that utility. One file per utility
(`api/v1/service-areas/<CODE>.json`, 141 files); `x-static-file` names the MERALCO
example. Region-level rows are an explicit fallback, not LGU-level confirmation.

200.description: One utility's coverage rows. Full response: api/v1/service-areas/MERALCO.json.

get.description:
Latest-month medians, means and ranges per customer class, reporting counts, island group
and the DOE workbook's own region label for all 18 PSA PSGC regions. Aggregates use
published cells only and exclude NDA, missing and invalid values.

get.summary: One region plus its member utilities
get.description:
One region's aggregates plus every member utility with its latest-month values and
explicit states. PSGC codes come from `/regions.json`; an unknown code is simply not a
file (the host returns 404). There is one file per region
(`api/v1/regions/<psgc>.json`, 18 files); `x-static-file` names the NCR example.

get.summary: Source registry: the DOE workbook and its checksums
get.description:
The single upstream source record: canonical DOE URL, workbook URL and sheet id,
retrieval timestamp and extraction method, per-tab SHA-256 and byte counts, archived raw
snapshots, licence status and provenance notes. Every value in this API resolves to this
record and to a tab checksum.

The full source record for one `source_id`. This snapshot has exactly one upstream source,
`SRC-DOE-RATES`; unknown ids are simply not a file (the host returns 404). There is one
file per source (`api/v1/sources/<source_id>.json`); `x-static-file` names the only one.

200.description: One source record. Full response: api/v1/sources/SRC-DOE-RATES.json.

StaticNotFound.description:
The static host returns its own 404 page for a path it does not serve; this snapshot does
not emit a JSON error body. A JSON error envelope with machine-readable slugs
(`bad_request`, `not_found`, `method_not_allowed`, ...) is reserved for a future dynamic
deployment, which can adopt it without changing the success payloads.

MonthToken.description: Billing month as YYYY-MM, as labelled in the source workbook.

Status.description: Explicit source state for one utility/class/month cell: published (a numeric rate exists), nda ("No Data Available" as published by the source), missing (the month column exists but the cell is blank / not yet published) or invalid (the cell failed extraction validation). null never means zero.

RateClass.description: Customer class; generation is the DOE workbook's blended generation charge.

NullableNumber.description: A number, or null when the source does not publish a value.

NullableMonthToken.description: A YYYY-MM month, or null when the series has no published month.

Licence.description: Licence status of the upstream data. The DOE workbook states no explicit reuse licence, so this API asserts none: name is "Not stated by publisher", url is null, and reuse terms are to be confirmed with DOE in writing.

note.description: Plain-language explanation of the licence status.

url.description: Always null: no licence URL exists for the upstream data.

Disclaimer.description: One disclaimer paragraph. Keep it with any figure republished from this API; `url` points at the Disclaimers section of the API documentation.

text.description: The disclaimer text, reproduced from the API documentation.

SourceRef.description: Compact source reference repeated in every response meta.

canonical_url.description: The DOE page that embeds the public workbook.

retrieved_at.description: When this snapshot was retrieved from the source.

SourceTab.description: One tab of the DOE workbook, with the SHA-256 of the exact CSV bytes retrieved.

gid.description: Google Sheet tab gid used in the CSV export URL.

RawSnapshot.description: Archived raw CSV bytes for one source tab, kept in the repository.

path.description: Repository-relative path of the archived raw CSV.

allOf.description: The complete source record published at /sources.json.

workbook_url.description: The public Google Sheet the four CSVs were exported from.

DataFile.description: A tidy seed CSV that ships beside the API (path relative to draft/).

CoverageDetail.description: Strongest published coverage level for a utility: lgu (LGU-level rows), barangay (barangay-level rows only) or region (a single region-level fallback row; no LGU-level service area is sourced).

note.description: Attribution / share-alike note for this coverage source.

ServiceAreaMeta.description: Derived service-area coverage context repeated in every response meta: how many utilities have LGU-level, barangay-level or region-level coverage, and which coverage sources (with licences) back the layer. Coverage is derived data, not a DOE rate publication.

CoverageCheck.description: One coverage validation check as recorded at build/ingest time.

ServiceAreaStats.description: Aggregate coverage statistics derived from the coverage seed. Keys are published as supplied by the seed (additional keys are allowed as the seed grows).

CoverageSummary.description: Compact coverage block published on registry rows and list endpoints.

allOf.description: Full coverage block for one utility: provinces, LGU PSGC codes, barangays and a note.

CoverageUsedFor.description: How many published rows/utilities a coverage source backs.

CoverageSource.description: One source of the service-area coverage layer, with its own licence and attribution (public law, CC BY-SA where OSM Wiki / Wikipedia tables are used, or the DOE workbook terms for the region-level fallback).

ServiceAreaRow.description: One published coverage row: a covered LGU (area_level: lgu), a covered barangay (area_level: barangay), or a single region-level fallback row (area_level: region). Every row carries its source_id.

ServiceAreaTally.description: Coverage tally published on list endpoints.

ServiceAreaDocument.description: The service_area block of /meta.json: coverage stats, sources, checks and files.

Meta.description: Response metadata repeated in every envelope. States the API and dataset versions, the latest published month, the rate-data source, attribution, licence status, all five disclaimers and the derived service-area coverage context (detail counts and the coverage sources with their licences). `count` is the number of primary records in `data` (rows for a list, months for the month series, 1 for a single record).

dataset_version.description: Retrieval date; changes with every new snapshot.

attribution.description: Attribution text to carry with republished figures.

StateArrays.description: Counts aligned to the months array in MonthsData.

Conflict.description: One source disagreement and how it was resolved.

canonical.description: The value published after resolution; "CONFLICT" marks an unresolved 2-2 split.

claims.description: Per-tab claims; shape depends on the conflict type.

variants.description: Tab-specific name variants for name_variant rows.

RateClassStats.description: Summary statistics for one customer class in the latest (or anchor) month, over published values only.

file.description: Relative path of the per-class file.

RateRow.description: One utility in a latest-month class file.

ClassValues.description: One value per customer class; null where the cell is not published.

UtilitySummary.description: Compact registry row: identity, geography, latest/previous month cells and their states.

code.description: Stable slug used by this dataset, not an official DOE/ERC/NEA identifier.

name_variants.description: Tab-specific alternative names keyed by customer class.

grid_conflict.description: Present when the tabs split 2-2 on grid connection; null otherwise.

on_grid.description: Whether the source tabs agree the utility is on-grid. Null when the tabs split 2-2 (see grid_conflict, and grid: CONFLICT).

data_status.description: Utility-level summary of the latest month: published (residential value exists), partial (some classes published), nda (no latest-month values).

source_row.description: 1-based row in each DOE workbook tab.

SeriesClass.description: One customer-class series grouped by explicit source state. `published` maps month to PHP/kWh; `nda`, `missing` and `invalid` list the months with those states. The four states together cover every month in `coverage.months_total` exactly once.

published.description: Published values: YYYY-MM -> PHP per kWh.

RegionRow.description: One PSGC region with latest-month aggregates over published cells only.

sheet_label.description: Region label as it appears in the DOE workbook.

reporting.description: Utilities with a published residential value in the latest month.

AvailabilityChange.description: One cell whose explicit state changed between the two months.

Envelope.description: The response envelope shared by every data file: meta, data and next_cursor.

data.description: Response payload; its concrete schema is the endpoint-specific Response schema.

next_cursor.description: Always null: this static snapshot has no pagination or query layer. The field is reserved so a future dynamic deployment can paginate without breaking clients.

ErrorResponse.description: Reserved for a future dynamic deployment, not emitted by this static snapshot. Follows the BetterGov Budget API error convention: a machine-readable slug plus a human-readable message.

error.description: Machine-readable slug: bad_request, bad_cursor, not_found, method_not_allowed, not_loaded, query_failed.

x-static-api.note: Static read-only snapshot: every path is a JSON file; no query parameters, no auth; next_cursor is always null.

changes: Initial static snapshot: 17 routes, 176 JSON files, 141 utilities, 18 regions, 107 month columns (2018-01 to 2026-11; latest published month 2026-10).
Contract version 1.0: envelope {meta, data, next_cursor} with explicit NDA/missing/invalid states and no imputed values.
Licence status published as "Not stated by publisher"; upstream reuse terms to be confirmed with DOE.

v1.1 coverage layer (additive to contract 1.0): 19 routes over 318 JSON files. Added GET /v1/service-areas.json (registry + source provenance) and GET /v1/service-areas/<CODE>.json (141 per-utility files); a compact coverage summary on /v1/utilities rows and the full service_area block on /v1/utilities/<CODE>; coverage stats/sources in meta, index, health, validation and sources; and a fifth disclaimer, disclaimer-coverage. Coverage is derived data, not a DOE rate publication.
The wire envelope (meta/data/next_cursor) and every rate endpoint are unchanged by the coverage layer.
